learning.title: Reporting privacy-suppressed dimensions preserve aggregate metrics
learning.claim: The YouTube Reporting API anonymizes some dimension values below privacy thresholds as NULL, ZZ, or US-ZZ, while preserving aggregate metrics in those rows; actual thresholds may change.
learning.decision: REPORT_PRIVACY_SUPPRESSION_GATE: Treat NULL in privacy-suppressed traffic-source, age, gender or subscribed-status dimensions and ZZ/US-ZZ in geography dimensions as anonymized aggregate buckets, not malformed or missing rows. Preserve their numeric metrics in totals while keeping the underlying dimension unknown; never reconstruct hidden identities, locations, search terms or thresholds. Keep this rule distinct from header-only zero-data CSV handling. This is a documented ingestion rule, not proof of owned-channel Reporting API access or deployed parser behavior.
learning.next_measurement: On a permitted owned-channel Reporting API read, use header-mapped CSV parsing and compare aggregate totals with and without anonymized rows; verify no suppressed dimension is imputed. Until then production integration remains unverified.
failure_history: 2026-10-08 earlier candidate promotion write was blocked before a commit; no persistent record was established.
fallback_history: Without authorized Reporting API CSV access, preserve this as an official documentation-based ingestion rule and do not invent channel-level data or a passing integration test.
